findings.title: Transport settlement is treated as physical Core reader drain
findings.criterion: ADR-0029 requires real cooperative cancellation and owned reader/lease release, with the supported maximum-source cancellation boundary <=1 second. The task-owned source-viewing contract and PdfDocumentViewer.stop comments additionally promise actual admitted-reader drain before replacement decoder/range admission.
findings.evidence: ViewerByteSession.drain waits only Promise.allSettled over port.range promises. Native owned HTTP reads return cancellation as soon as their authorization latch fails, and cancel_core posts a route whose service implementation only sets request.stop. DocumentViewerRangePool.read raises for a cancelled waiter before group.done; the physical group owner closes later in _run. Therefore an IPC promise may settle while the old Core authentication/stream/transaction remains active. PdfDocumentViewer.ensure can then create a replacement decoder after this transport-only drain resolves. No terminal owner acknowledgement crosses the reviewed native protocol. Existing scheduler/fair project locks prevent simultaneous physical reads, but do not make early IPC settlement proof of drain or enforce the claimed replacement deadline.
findings.reproduction: Hold the real original authentication loop after a bounded frame has entered, cancel its native/renderer operation, allow the native IPC request to settle while retaining the held Core owner, then request a replacement render. At this candidate, drain can resolve and replacement decoder construction can occur before the held owner is released. Observe the actual reader registry/transaction and replacement admission, not only a UI callback or synthetic byte-port promise. This reviewer did not execute that regression; the defect is established by the candidate control-flow inspection.
findings.smallestClosure: Bind cancellation/drain acknowledgement to the exact root/project/native-session/request and physical terminal state. Last-member cancellation must not acknowledge drain before the owned stream/transaction closes; surviving coalesced followers keep independent authorization and ownership. Deadline expiry or unknown/failed acknowledgement must explicitly deny replacement. Persist failed/unknown drain state in the byte-session owner: Promise.allSettled or pending removal must not erase it.
findings.requiredRegression: A held real encrypted-read/native transport case proves no replacement decoder/range enters before actual close; a >1-second held owner returns explicit drain-pending denial; failed/lost acknowledgements remain poisoned after pending removal; early cancellation/late Core registration cannot turn an absent request into a false drain; live exact duplicate followers survive one member's cancellation with fresh delivery authority.
findings.proposedParentClosure: The parent proposed a Core terminal event, acknowledgement after participation ends and last-member physical owner closes, <=1-second or drain-pending denial, renderer acknowledgement waiting and poisoned unresolved drain, while preserving followers and the one-active scheduler. This direction addresses the finding if it also handles absent/early/lost cancellation and persists failure after pending removal.
